doc_description: Pfizer Inc.’s SEC Form 10‑Q for Q2 2023 (quarter ended July 2, 2023) reports revenues of $12.7B (down 54% year over year) and diluted EPS of $0.41 driven by steep declines in Comirnaty and Paxlovid, near‑breakeven operating cash flow, and the issuance of $31B of new debt to help finance the pending Seagen acquisition, with disclosure controls deemed effective.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- Document type and period: Pfizer Inc. Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 2, 2023 (Commission File No. 1-3619), filed with the U.S. SEC.
- Company and securities details: Delaware corporation (EIN 13-5315170), principal office at 66 Hudson Boulevard East, New York, NY 10001-2192; phone (212) 733-2323. Securities listed on NYSE: Common Stock (PFE) and 1.000% Notes due 2027 (PFE27). Shares outstanding as of August 4, 2023: 5,645,959,570.
- Compliance status: Has filed all required reports and submitted all required interactive data files; classified as a large accelerated filer; not an emerging growth company; not a shell company.
- Table of contents overview:
  - Part I: Financial Information—Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements (Income, Comprehensive Income, Balance Sheets, Equity, Cash Flows) and Notes; Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A); Market Risk; Controls and Procedures.
  - Part II: Other Information—Legal Proceedings; Risk Factors; Unregistered Sales/Use of Proceeds; Other Information; Exhibits; Signature.
- Defined terms and scope notes: Glossary of abbreviations and entities (e.g., Comirnaty, Paxlovid, BioNTech, MD&A, EUA, etc.); explanation of differing quarter-end dates for U.S. vs. ex-U.S. subsidiaries; rounding notes; trademarks; caution that website/social media content is not incorporated by reference; clinical study and regulatory-approval caveats; EUA disclosures for certain COVID-19 products.
- Key financial statement included (unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income):
  - Three months ended: Revenues $12.734B vs. $27.742B (prior year); Net income attributable to Pfizer common shareholders $2.327B vs. $9.906B; Basic EPS $0.41 vs. $1.77; Diluted EPS $0.41 vs. $1.73.
  - Six months ended: Revenues $31.015B vs. $53.402B; Net income attributable to Pfizer common shareholders $7.870B vs. $17.769B; Basic EPS $1.40 vs. $3.17; Diluted EPS $1.38 vs. $3.10.
  - Expense highlights (Q2 2023): Cost of sales $3.237B; SI&A $3.497B; R&D $2.648B; Amortization of intangibles $1.184B; Other (income)/deductions, net $(0.347)B; Income from continuing operations before tax $2.269B; Tax benefit $(0.071)B.

structure.title: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income
structure.heading: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income
structure.summary:
- Part I – Financial Information, Item 1 presents Pfizer’s unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income and Comprehensive Income for the three and six months ended July 2, 2023 and July 3, 2022.
- Income statement highlights:
  - Revenues declined sharply year over year (Q2: $12.7B vs $27.7B; YTD: $31.0B vs $53.4B).
  - Cost of sales fell materially versus 2022; SG&A and amortization of intangibles increased; R&D was slightly lower in Q2 but roughly flat YTD; acquired IPR&D was minimal in Q2 2023 vs higher prior-year periods.
  - Other (income)/deductions swung to net income in 2023 from net deductions in 2022; Q2 2023 reflected a tax benefit.
  - Income from continuing operations and net income attributable to Pfizer declined significantly (Q2 net income to shareholders: $2.33B vs $9.91B; YTD: $7.87B vs $17.77B).
  - EPS decreased (Q2 basic/diluted: $0.41/$0.41 vs $1.77/$1.73; YTD basic/diluted: $1.40/$1.38 vs $3.17/$3.10). Discontinued operations were immaterial. Weighted-average shares were slightly higher in 2023.
  - Note indicates certain amounts are exclusive of amortization of intangible assets.
- Comprehensive income highlights:
  - Other comprehensive income (OCI) turned positive in 2023 (Q2: +$184M; YTD: +$196M) versus losses in 2022, driven by favorable foreign currency translation and derivative OCI, partially offset by available-for-sale securities and pension-related reclassifications.
  - Comprehensive income attributable to Pfizer was $2.51B in Q2 2023 and $8.07B YTD, both below prior-year periods.
  - Footnotes reference reclassification adjustments into Other (income)/deductions—net and Cost of sales.

structure.title: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income
structure.heading: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income
structure.start_phrase: Reclassified into Other (income)/deductions—net and Cost of sales.
structure.summary:
- Contents: Unaudited condensed consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income for the three and six months ended July 2, 2023 and July 3, 2022, and Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets as of July 2, 2023 and December 31, 2022, for Pfizer Inc. and subsidiaries.
- Comprehensive income highlights:
  - Net income before allocation to noncontrolling interests fell sharply year over year: $2,338M vs $9,911M for Q2; $7,894M vs $17,781M for the six months.
  - Other comprehensive income (OCI) swung positive in 2023: $184M in Q2 2023 vs $(968)M in Q2 2022; $196M for six months 2023 vs $(1,228)M in 2022.
  - OCI components include:
    - Foreign currency translation adjustments: positive in 2023 (Q2: +$242M; YTD: +$343M) vs negative in 2022.
    - Derivative instruments: net unrealized gains with reclassification adjustments, yielding Q2 net +$55M (109 − 163) and YTD +$251M.
    - Available-for-sale securities: Q2 net +$42M vs $(232)M prior year; YTD $(379)M vs $(132)M, reflecting sizable reclassification losses included in net income.
    - Pension/postretirement reclassification adjustments: negative to OCI (Q2 $(37)M; YTD $(72)M).
  - Tax on OCI: small provision/benefit (Q2 +$9M; YTD $(53)M).
  - Comprehensive income attributable to Pfizer Inc.: $2,514M in Q2 2023 vs $8,943M in Q2 2022; $8,072M YTD 2023 vs $16,546M YTD 2022.
- Balance sheet highlights (July 2, 2023 vs Dec 31, 2022):
  - Assets rose to $220.2B from $197.2B, driven by:
    - Cash and cash equivalents up to $2.6B (from $0.4B) and short-term investments up to $42.2B (from $22.3B).
    - PP&E increased to $17.5B; identifiable intangibles declined to $41.4B (amortization); goodwill slightly higher at $51.6B.
  - Liabilities increased to $120.9B (from $101.3B):
    - Long-term debt grew significantly to $61.4B (from $32.9B).
    - Total current liabilities decreased to $34.6B (from $42.1B), with lower deferred revenues and other current liabilities.
  - Equity increased to $99.3B (Pfizer Inc. shareholders’ equity $99.0B), with accumulated other comprehensive loss modestly improved (from $(8.3)B to $(8.1)B); noncontrolling interests at $274M.
- Notes/reclassifications: Certain OCI reclassification adjustments were recorded into Other (income)/deductions—net and Cost of sales (referenced Note 7E); financials are unaudited and accompanied by notes.

structure.title: Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets
structure.heading: Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets
structure.summary:
- Unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets for Pfizer Inc. and subsidiaries as of July 2, 2023 and December 31, 2022 (in millions), detailing assets, liabilities, and equity.
- Assets highlights: Total assets increased to $220.2B from $197.2B, driven primarily by a sharp rise in cash and cash equivalents plus short-term investments ($44.8B vs. $22.7B), higher inventories, and higher property, plant and equipment; identifiable intangible assets declined (amortization), goodwill was roughly flat.
- Liabilities highlights: Total liabilities rose to $120.9B from $101.3B, mainly from an increase in long-term debt ($61.4B vs. $32.9B). Current liabilities decreased overall, with lower other current liabilities and deferred revenues, while income taxes payable increased.
- Equity highlights: Total equity increased to $99.3B from $95.9B. Retained earnings grew ($128.8B vs. $125.7B), accumulated other comprehensive loss improved slightly, and treasury stock was largely unchanged. Noncontrolling interests were modest ($274M).
- Condensed consolidated statements of equity (quarter and year-to-date):
  - Quarter ended July 2, 2023 vs. prior-year quarter: net income of $2.33B vs. $9.91B; other comprehensive income turned positive; dividends declared of $0.82/share vs. $0.80/share in 2022; routine share-based payment impacts to additional paid-in capital and treasury stock.
  - Six months ended July 2, 2023 vs. six months ended July 3, 2022: year-to-date net income of $7.87B vs. $17.77B; dividends of $0.82/share vs. $0.80/share; 2023 shows no share repurchases, while 2022 included $2.0B of common stock purchases.
- Presentation includes “Commitments and Contingencies” and references accompanying notes.

- Provides unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the six months ended July 2, 2023 and July 3, 2022:

  - Financing activities:

    - Debt repayments, dividends paid ($4,618 million in 2023; $4,493 million in 2022), no 2023 buybacks vs. $2,000 million in 2022
    - Net cash provided: $24,403 million (2023) vs. net cash used $(4,058) million (2022)
  - Net increase in cash and restricted cash: $2,229 million (ending at $2,698 million) in 2023 vs. decrease of $(159) million (ending at $1,824 million) in 2022

structure.title: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
structure.heading: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
structure.summary:
- Provides Pfizer’s unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the six months ended July 2, 2023 and July 3, 2022, plus supplemental cash flow information.
- Operating activities: Net cash provided was $4 million in 1H23 (vs. $14.7 billion in 1H22), as sizable unfavorable changes in working capital offset $7.9 billion of net income and noncash add-backs (e.g., $3.1 billion depreciation and amortization).
- Investing activities: Net cash used was $22.2 billion (vs. $10.7 billion), driven by significant net purchases of short-term investments and higher capex; minimal acquisition outflows in 2023 vs. larger outflows in 2022.
- Financing activities: Net cash provided was $24.4 billion (vs. net use of $4.1 billion), primarily from $30.8 billion of new long-term debt; dividends of $4.6 billion; no 2023 share repurchases (vs. $2.0 billion in 2022).
- Net change in cash: Increase of $2.2 billion, ending cash and restricted cash of $2.7 billion.
- Supplemental cash flow info: Income taxes paid $2.0 billion; interest paid $0.8 billion; interest rate hedge cash flows $31 million.
- Notes—Basis of presentation: Prepared in conformity with U.S. GAAP; interim reporting conventions; normal recurring adjustments included; international subsidiaries’ fiscal quarter-end differs from U.S. subsidiaries.
- Segment reporting: Two operating segments (Biopharma and Business Innovation); Biopharma is the only reportable segment; certain prior-period reclassifications to conform presentation.
- Business development: Agreement to acquire Seagen for ~$43 billion enterprise value; to be financed substantially by $31 billion of long-term debt issued in May 2023 plus other sources; shareholder approval obtained; expected closing late 2023/early 2024 pending regulatory approvals.
- New accounting standards adopted in 2023: Enhanced disclosures for supplier finance programs; application of reference rate reform expedients to maintain hedge accounting during LIBOR transition through December 31, 2024.
- Revenues and trade receivables: Sales channels outlined—most products to wholesalers; Paxlovid primarily to government agencies and distributors; vaccines sold to U.S. federal government and other providers; outside the U.S., primarily to governmental and non-governmental institutions.
- Deductions from revenues: Accruals for rebates, chargebacks, allowances, returns, and discounts; total accrued rebates and other sales-related accruals of $7.0 billion at July 2, 2023 (vs. $6.7 billion at Dec 31, 2022), including a $1.236 billion reserve against trade receivables.

structure.title: Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.heading: Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.start_phrase:
We prepared these condensed consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP, consistent in all material respects with those applied in our
2022 Form 10-K.
structure.summary:
- Scope and basis: Unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP, consistent with the 2022 Form 10-K; certain interim disclosures condensed/omitted. Pfizer operates through two segments (Biopharma—reportable; and Business Innovation), with reclassifications made to conform prior-period segment presentation.

- Major business development: Agreement to acquire Seagen for ~$43 billion (approved by Seagen shareholders; expected close late 2023/early 2024, subject to regulatory approvals). Financing includes $31 billion of senior unsecured notes issued in May 2023, with remaining funding from cash and short-term financing.

- New accounting standards: Adoption of supplier finance program disclosure standard (Note 8C) and optional expedients for reference rate reform to ease LIBOR transition for hedge accounting through December 31, 2024.

- Revenue and receivables: Product/customer mix outlined (e.g., Paxlovid primarily to governments/distributors; vaccines in U.S. to federal government, wholesalers, providers, pharmacies). Sales deductions and related accruals totaled $6.99 billion at July 2, 2023. Trade receivables measured with pooled expected credit loss approach; changes in allowances immaterial for the periods.

- M&A and portfolio: 2022 acquisitions of GBT ($5.7B consideration; IPR&D and developed technology intangibles), Biohaven ($11.8B; developed tech and IPR&D; inventory step-up), and Arena ($6.6B; substantial IPR&D). Allocations for GBT and Biohaven provisional; Arena final in Q1 2023. Discontinued operations reflect post-close adjustments and agreements (e.g., Viatris spin-off).

- Equity-method investment: 32% stake in Haleon; carrying value $11.2B and fair value $12.1B at July 2, 2023. Share of Haleon earnings recorded on one-quarter lag; FX translation impacts AOCI.

- R&D funding: Up to $550M from Blackstone (2023–2026) to co-fund specified development costs; recognized as reduction to R&D expense over related periods. Approval-based and sales-based milestones to be capitalized as intangibles upon achievement; royalties recorded in cost of sales.

- Restructuring and productivity: Ongoing “Transforming to a More Focused Company” program (initiated 2019), substantially complete by end of 2023; cumulative costs ~$3.8B (about 85% incurred). Q2 and YTD 2023 include restructuring charges, transaction, integration, implementation costs, and additional depreciation; reconciliation of restructuring accruals provided.

- Other income/deductions: Net interest expense decreased YTD due to higher interest income on invested debt proceeds; equity security fair value impacts (gains/losses) noted; legal matters; intangible asset impairments ($248M YTD) due to trial outcomes and forecast updates; equity-method income from Haleon; other income includes dividend income from investments (e.g., ViiV, Nimbus).

- Taxes: Effective tax rate was (3.1)% in Q2 2023 and 7.5% YTD, lower due to multi-jurisdiction tax resolutions and favorable mix of earnings. U.S. transition tax installments ongoing (through 2026). Audits active in multiple jurisdictions.

- AOCI: Changes driven by FX translation, derivatives, available-for-sale securities, and benefit plan reclassifications; overall AOCI loss narrowed.

- Financial instruments and liquidity:
  - Fair value disclosures for investments and derivatives; significant increase in short-term investments (money market funds, government securities).
  - Long-term debt rose to ~$61B carrying amount after issuing $31B in May 2023 (various maturities 2025–2063; WAEIR ~4.93%; special mandatory redemption tied to Seagen closing). Hedging activities summarized (FX and interest rate risk), cash flow and net investment hedge results, collateral positions.
  - Short-term borrowings include current maturities and collateral-related amounts.

- Credit risk: Concentrations in wholesalers/governments for receivables; investment exposure mainly to U.S./developed sovereigns and money market funds; derivative counterparties subject to daily collateralization.

- Working capital and supplier finance: Inventories increased to $10.3B (plus $5.9B noncurrent), primarily Paxlovid and supply recovery; no recoverability issues expected. Amounts payable to BioNTech for Comirnaty gross profit split declined as deliveries moderated. Supplier finance program payables outstanding were $779M.

- Intangible assets: Net identifiable intangibles $41.4B (finite-lived developed technology, brands, licensing; indefinite-lived brands/IPR&D). Activity includes U.S. approvals driving transfers from IPR&D (e.g., Zavzpret, Ngenla), capitalized milestones, amortization, and impairments.

- Pensions/postretirement: Net periodic benefit credits/costs detailed; 2022 reflected remeasurement losses; 2023 contributions disclosed.

- EPS: Basic and diluted EPS computations presented; small number of anti-dilutive equivalents.

- Contingencies and commitments:
  - Extensive patent, product liability, commercial, and government investigation matters disclosed, including ongoing IP litigation around Comirnaty (various plaintiffs), Paxlovid, Abrysvo, Xeljanz, Ibrance, Mektovi, Eucrisa, Xtandi, Eliquis; product matters (asbestos, Effexor, Lipitor, EpiPen, PPIs, Docetaxel, Zantac, Chantix); commercial/environmental (Monsanto/Pharmacia legacy, Bound Brook site), Anti-Terrorism Act/Iraq MOH contracts, Viatris securities litigation; multiple U.S./ex-U.S. government inquiries (antitrust, FCPA, manufacturing, Meridian, Biohaven, Xeljanz).
  - Guarantees/indemnifications typical for transactions and collaborations (e.g., BioNTech COVID-19 partnership), and guarantees of subsidiary debt; fair value of obligations not material.

- Segment and revenue information:
  - Biopharma is the sole reportable segment; Business Innovation includes Pfizer CentreOne (CDMO and API supply) and Pfizer Ignite (R&D services). Company-wide assets managed centrally.
  - Sharp year-over-year revenue declines across geographies due to lower COVID-19 products (Comirnaty, Paxlovid); notable performance from Eliquis, Prevnar family, Vyndaqel, oncology portfolio, and recently acquired brands (Nurtec ODT/Vydura, Oxbryta).
  - Product revenue table provided for major brands across Primary Care, Specialty Care, Oncology, and Business Innovation.
  - EC-Pfizer/BioNTech contract amendment rephases and reduces EU COVID-19 vaccine volumes through 2026.
  - Remaining performance obligations for Comirnaty supply contracts approx. $9B (2023–2026); Comirnaty deferred revenue $1.2B (mostly current) as of July 2, 2023.

structure.title: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase:
The following MD&A is intended to assist the reader in understanding our financial condition and results of operations, including an evaluation of the amounts
and certainty of cash flows from operations and from outside sources, and is provided as a supplement to and should be read in conjunction with the condensed
consolidated financial statements and related notes in Item 1. Financial Statements in this Form 10-Q.
structure.summary:
- Scope and purpose: MD&A supplements the financial statements, explains period-over-period “operational” variances excluding FX, and provides outlook.
- Business overview and strategy: Pfizer operates two segments (Biopharma—reportable—and Business Innovation). In 2023 it is investing further in R&D and SI&A to support near- and long-term growth, launches, COVID-19 commercialization, pipeline programs, and acquired assets.
- Organizational changes: Ongoing “Transforming to a More Focused Company” program to optimize R&D, reduce costs/cycle times, prioritize differentiated areas, and expand external innovation. As of July 2023, oncology discovery-to-late development consolidated into a new Oncology R&D platform; other therapeutic areas consolidated in Pfizer Research and Development.
- Upjohn separation: About $700 million in total expected costs; roughly 90% incurred through Q2 2023.
- Business development:
  - Proposed acquisition of Seagen; $31 billion of senior unsecured notes issued in May 2023 to support financing.
  - Agreement to sell/license early-stage rare disease gene therapy portfolio to Alexion (up to $1 billion plus tiered royalties), consistent with pivot to new platforms (e.g., mRNA, in vivo gene editing).
  - Collaboration with Flagship Pioneering: each to invest $50 million upfront to develop up to 10 single-asset programs; up to $700 million in milestones plus royalties per program.
  - Termination of Bavencio alliance with Merck KGaA; from Q3 2023, Pfizer to receive 15% royalty on Bavencio net sales; Merck KGaA assumes commercialization and future R&D control.
- Performance highlights:
  - Q2 2023 revenues $12.7 billion, down 54% (operationally -53%), driven by declines in Paxlovid and Comirnaty; ex-COVID-19 products grew 5% operationally (notably Nurtec ODT/Vydura, Oxbryta, Vyndaqel; offset by Inflectra U.S. and Ibrance declines).
  - H1 2023 revenues $31.0 billion, down 42% (operationally -40%); ex-COVID-19 products up 5% operationally (Nurtec ODT/Vydura, Oxbryta, Vyndaqel, Eliquis, Sulperazon in China; offset by Ibrance).
  - 2023 total revenue guidance: $67–$70 billion (operational decline vs. 2022), mainly due to lower COVID product sales, partly offset by non-COVID growth, new launches, and recent acquisitions.
  - Income from continuing operations before taxes decreased significantly in Q2 and H1 due to lower revenues and higher SI&A, partly offset by lower cost of sales and equity security gains.
- Operating environment and risks:
  - Intellectual property: Moderate revenue impact from expiries expected 2023–2025; more significant from 2026–2030; ongoing defense of patents.
  - Pricing and access: Global payer pressures; U.S. IRA impact still being assessed; potential changes to Medicaid and 340B could be material.
  - Supply and manufacturing: Tornado damaged the Rocky Mount, NC sterile injectables warehouse in July 2023; production areas largely intact; actions underway to reorder supplies, secure temporary warehousing, and explore alternate manufacturing; financial impact under evaluation. Industry-wide nitrosamine assessments have led to past recalls and may lead to further actions.
  - Macroeconomic considerations and Russia/Ukraine conflict: Exposure to Russia/Ukraine <1% of revenues/assets; monitoring ongoing risks.
- COVID-19 business transition and outlook:
  - Continued evaluation of Comirnaty and Paxlovid against variants; development of variant-adapted and next-generation vaccines/therapies and combinations.
  - Transition of U.S. sales of Comirnaty and Paxlovid to traditional commercial markets expected in H2 2023; international markets largely remain under government contracts in 2023, with commercial transitions starting in 2024.
  - 2023 forecasts (as of Aug 1, 2023): Comirnaty ~$13.5 billion (-64% vs 2022), gross profit split with BioNTech; Paxlovid ~$8 billion (-58% vs 2022); revenues expected to trough in 2023 and potentially grow in 2024; significant uncertainties remain.
- Geographic revenues: Sharp declines in both U.S. and international markets primarily due to COVID-19 product decreases; emerging markets down markedly (Q2 -53%; H1 -45%) mainly from lower Comirnaty (partly offset by Paxlovid growth and Sulperazon in H1).
- Revenue deductions: Deductions tied to volume, mix, and contractual/legislative rebates and discounts; largest items include chargebacks, performance-based rebates, and sales allowances.
- Product revenue trends (Q2/H1 2023):
  - Comirnaty: Q2 down ~83%; H1 down ~79%.
  - Paxlovid: Q2 down ~98% (no U.S. Q2 sales ahead of commercial transition); H1 down ~56%, with earlier strength in China.
  - Eliquis: Low single-digit global growth; U.S. growth offset by LOE/generic pressure internationally.
  - Prevnar family: Mixed; adult growth (Prevnar 20) offset by U.S. pediatric softness ahead of Prevnar 20 transition and competition.
  - Ibrance: Declines due to competition, lower clinical trial purchases, and planned price cuts in some markets.
  - Vyndaqel family: Strong growth from ATTR-CM uptake.
  - Xeljanz: Q2 up in U.S. on favorable mix/price; H1 down on lower volumes tied to prescribing shifts.
  - Xtandi and Inlyta: Modest growth/mixed performance; Nurtec ODT/Vydura contributed post-Biohaven acquisition; Oxbryta added growth.
- Costs and expenses:
  - Cost of sales decreased significantly on lower COVID sales and reduced Comirnaty write-offs; mix shift favorable.
  - SI&A increased on marketing for recent/launch products and preparation for Paxlovid commercial launch; partly offset by lower U.S. healthcare reform fees tied to lower COVID sales.
  - R&D: Q2 lower from reduced COVID spending; H1 roughly flat with higher investment in acquired assets, vaccines, and late-stage programs offsetting COVID reductions.
  - Amortization higher due to Biohaven and GBT acquisitions.
  - Other income/deductions improved vs. prior year on equity security gains and pension credits.
  - Effective tax rate lower; Q2 showed a tax benefit; details in Note 5.
- Restructuring and productivity: Program-wide net savings targets include ~$1.4B (commercial strategy, 2022–2024), ~$550M (manufacturing network, 2020–2023), and ~$2.3B (end-to-end R&D, 2023–2025). Certain qualifying costs excluded from non-GAAP results.
- Product development and regulatory:
  - COVID-19 vaccines: U.S. EUA harmonization to bivalent; sBLA for BA.4/BA.5 bivalent; filings for XBB.1.5-adapted monovalent in U.S./EU/Japan; multiple EU/Japan approvals/variations across age groups.
  - Key approvals/filings: Paxlovid full approval (U.S. high-risk adults); Prevnar 20 pediatric (U.S.); Ngenla (U.S./EU/JP pediatric GHD); Litfulo/Ritfulo (alopecia areata U.S./Japan); Zavzpret (intranasal migraine U.S.); Myfembree (endometriosis pain U.S.); Abrysvo (RSV older adults U.S.; filings for maternal and other regions); ABCWY meningococcal vaccine filing; elranatamab filings; Talzenna+Xtandi approval/filings; fidanacogene elaparvovec filings (hemophilia B).
  - Late-stage pipeline spans oncology (e.g., vepdegestrant), infectious diseases (ABCWY, C. difficile, influenza mRNA, Lyme VLA15), gene therapies (hemophilia A/B, DMD), hematology (marstacimab), rare diseases (inclacumab), and others.
- Non-GAAP reporting: Adjusted Income/Adjusted diluted EPS exclude amortization, certain acquisition-related items, discontinued operations, and specified significant items; reconciliations provided; measures used for performance evaluation and incentive compensation, with noted limitations.
- Cash flows, liquidity, and capital resources:
  - H1 2023 operating cash flow near breakeven due to lower earnings and timing of receipts/payments (including BioNTech profit split) and fewer advances.
  - Investing outflows increased largely from higher net purchases of short-term investments.
  - Financing inflows driven by $31B debt issuance for Seagen; strong liquidity with access to credit facilities; commercial paper and debt carry high-grade ratings (Moody’s A1, negative outlook; S&P A+, stable).
  - Capital allocation: Quarterly dividend of $0.41; no share repurchases YTD; no plan to monetize Haleon stake for Seagen financing.
- Accounting standards: Recently issued guidance on equity security sale restrictions expected to be immaterial; policies and critical estimates unchanged from 2022 10-K.
- Forward-looking statements and risks: Extensive risk factors cited, including R&D outcomes, regulatory decisions, pricing/IRA impacts, competitive and generic pressures, supply chain and manufacturing disruptions (including Rocky Mount tornado), COVID-19 demand and market transition risks, macroeconomic/geopolitical uncertainties (including Russia/Ukraine), IP challenges and litigation, cybersecurity, tax/regulatory changes, and execution/integration risks for business development (including Seagen).
- Controls and procedures: Disclosure controls and procedures deemed effective as of the period end.
